questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code makes sure the agent is talking to the intended server over TLS? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In TlsContextFactory, which store proves the agent's identity to the server and which decides whether the server is trusted?
choices: The trust store identifies the agent and the identity store validates the server
The identity store (key managers) supplies the agent's client certificate and key; the trust store (trust managers) holds the CAs used to validate the server
Both stores are used only to validate the server, and the agent authenticates with a password
The null SecureRandom passed to init supplies the certificate

questions.prompt: The block store accepts the TCP connection but then never sends anything during the TLS handshake. What happens in open()?
choices: It waits forever because connectTimeout only covers TCP connect
startHandshake fails with a SocketTimeoutException after about 30 seconds, because the socket read timeout was set before the handshake and the plain socket is closed
The handshake is retried automatically over TLS 1.2 after 5 seconds
It succeeds, because the protocol list has two entries

questions.prompt: uploadBlock compares the server's 32-byte acknowledgement to the SHA-256 of the data it sent. What does this add on top of TLS?
choices: It protects the bytes against tampering on the network, which TLS does not
It confirms that the server received and acknowledged exactly the bytes sent, catching truncation or corruption on the server side or a protocol mix-up that TLS would not detect
It encrypts the block so the server cannot read it
It replaces the need for client certificates
